# Fold tree: read pb in the selection cycle, register the tree adder operands

- `rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv` (RSUM/RSSQ fold tree only). New comb `tb_rdy[b]` (the old `tr_go` term) and `tb_oh = tb_rdy & ~(tb_rdy - 1)`. The `tr_go`/`tr_b` priority loop now tests `tb_rdy[b]`, so it gives the same result as before.
- New `always_comb` builds `oa_n[k]`/`ob_n[k]` as a one-hot AND-OR over the NTB buffers. Each buffer's candidate uses its own `tb_i[bb]`/`tb_n[bb]` addresses, with the same row/lane expressions as the old `oa`/`ob`.
- `oa_q`/`ob_q` are registered next to `is_*` (same `ent && red_act && is_sum` enable) and feed `u_tree`. The `oa`/`ob`/`ib` wires in `g_tree` are removed. `ia` stays, but only for `tr_m`.
- `is_*`, `tr_v_q`/`tr_dst_q`/`tr_b_q`, write-back, `tb_inf` and root push are unchanged, so fold latency and protocol are the same.
- Reviewer note: this relies on `pb` not changing, at the locations an issue reads, between selection (t) and the old read (t+1). The argument is in HYPOTHESIS.md and summarized in a comment above the new block.
- Checks: verilator lint is clean. These pass: `test_mlp_rtl[1]`, `test_attention_decode_rtl[1-8-2-100]`, `test_fuzz_single_slice[0,1]`, `test_lane_count_does_not_change_results[4,16]`.
- Not done: synthesis/timing and the full gates.
lesson: Fold-tree operand mux moved into the select cycle (per-buffer candidates + one-hot AND-OR, same latency): +2.4% fmax, +9.1% area. Replicating the mux across 4 buffers costs too much, don't retry.

title: Fold tree: register the pb operands and pay for it by removing the level-done and root-push cycles
hypothesis:
# Fold tree: register the pb operands and pay for it by removing the level-done and root-push cycles

Category: timing

## Motivation
The champion's critical path (5.48 ns logic, 108 MHz, target 110) is the RSUM/RSSQ fold-tree read.
It starts at `is_n[1]` (FDRE.C->Q at 0.40 ns) and runs through the `ib = ia + is_n` carry (1.14 ns).
It then passes about 9 LUT levels of the `pb[is_b][row][k]` / lane-crossing `ob` mux (1.79 -> 4.07 ns).
The last part is the tree `otpu_fadd`'s first stage: the ftz and the `b[30:0] > a[30:0]` compare
(`$14249`, 3 CARRY4s), the swap LUT3, and the exponent-difference carry (`39309`) into an FF.
About 3 ns of this is the pb read and about 2 ns is the adder's first stage. Earlier attempts show:
- Pre-registering the select/address bits (014914-s0, +1.5%) and pruning the mux (025910-s1,
  +2.9% fmax, +2.6% area) don't cut enough. The mux and the adder's first stage are still in one cycle.
- Registering the pb operands does cut the path. But 025450-s0 did it by adding a cycle to the tree
  loop (LT = LA+1). That adds 1 cycle per fold level (6 per row), so attention_decode fell to
  59.6% (< 60%). 025910-s0 tried to win that cycle back with a new `tb_w` countdown, and the
  extra compare logic cost fmax (104 MHz).

The current tree scheduler already wastes cycles that can absorb the extra register at no latency
cost. Per level: last group selected in c0, `is_*` registered, pb read + adder stage 1 in c1,
`tr_y` valid in c5, pb written and `tb_inf` decremented at the end of c5. Then `tb_inf == 0` in
c6, which triggers only the separate **level-done** step (`tb_n >>= 1, tb_i = 0`). The next level
is selected in c7. That is one idle bookkeeping cycle per level. Likewise, the root is pushed into
`rq` one cycle *after* its result is written to `pb[bb][0][0]` (in the level-done step), and it
goes through a 4:1 read of `pb[*][0][0]`.

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)
1. **Operand register.** In `g_tree`, register the mux outputs on `ent`: `oa_q <= oa; ob_q <= ob;`.
   The `u_tree` adder then takes `.a(oa_q), .b(ob_q)`. The tree loop becomes LT = LA + 1: the
   `tr_v_q / tr_dst_q / tr_b_q` delay lines get one more stage. The pb write-back, the `tb_inf`
   decrement and the root use index `LT-1` instead of `LA-1`.
2. **Advance the level at its last issue, not after it drains.** In the per-buffer loop, when
   `tr_go && tr_b == bb`:
   - if `tb_i[bb] + LANES >= tb_n[bb]`: set `tb_n[bb] <= tb_n[bb] >> 1; tb_i[bb] <= 0`,
   - else: `tb_i[bb] <= tb_i[bb] + LANES`.

   `is_i / is_n` still capture the values before the advance. The drain wait is already built into
   `tr_go`'s `!(tb_i == 0 && tb_inf != 0)` term, so the next level still waits for every write of
   this one. Delete the level-done block (`tb_i >= tb_n && tb_inf == 0 && ...`). After the n = 1
   level, `tb_n` becomes 0, so `tb_i < tb_n` stops further issues.
3. **Push the root straight from the adder.** Carry a `root` bit (`is_n == 1`) down the `tr_*_q`
   pipeline. When `tr_v_q[LT-1][0] && tr_r_q[LT-1]`:
   - `rq_v <= tr_y[0]`, `rq_a <= tb_dst[tr_b_q[LT-1]]`, `tb_act[tr_b_q[LT-1]] <= 0`, mark the queue valid.
   - The root is still written to `pb` as well (harmless).
4. **One-entry result queue.** `rq` is popped in every `ent` cycle in which it is non-empty and
   gets at most one push per cycle. So `rq_n` never exceeds 1, and the `32'(rn) < NTB` room check
   is always true. Replace `rq_v[NTB] / rq_a[NTB] / rq_h / rq_n` with a single `rq_v, rq_a, rq_vld`
   register. `cw_*` then reads `rq_v / rq_a` when `rq_vld`, and the pop logic keeps the same
   `rows_done` / `fin` rules. Only one root can land per cycle, so the `pushed` priority chain is
   no longer needed.

### Why the results and the timing stay the same
- **Same adds, same order.** Every tree add has the same operand pair, in the same (a, b) order,
  in the same level order. The same pb cells are read and written.
- **Operand registers have no read-after-write hazard.** A level's reads never touch a row that an
  earlier group of the same level writes (group g writes row g and reads rows g' >= g). The next
  level is still gated on `tb_inf == 0`.
- **The schedule is cycle-identical to the champion.** Last group selected in c0: `oa_q` loaded at
  the end of c1, adder stage 1 in c2, `tr_y` in c6, pb write and `tb_inf` decrement at the end of
  c6, `tb_inf == 0` in c7, next level selected in c7. That is the same c7 as today, because the
  removed level-done cycle absorbs the extra register.
- **Buffer eligibility is unchanged.** A buffer that is draining is ineligible in both versions
  (old: `tb_i >= tb_n`; new: `tb_i == 0 && tb_inf != 0`), so the arbitration order is unchanged.
- **The root timing is unchanged.** For the n = 1 level selected in c0: old push and `tb_act` clear
  at the end of c6; new at the end of c6, straight from `tr_y`. So the capture `stall`, the `rq`
  write-out, `done` and the whole RSUM/RSSQ timeline are unchanged cycle for cycle. The ISA order
  of operations and the port protocols are untouched, and the Qwen proxy and the kernel perf gates
  should not move.

## Expected
- **FF:** +512 (oa_q/ob_q, 8 lanes x 64) +~20 (one more tr_* stage, root bit) −~195 (3 of the 4 rq
  entries, rq_h/rq_n): about **+340 FF**.
- **LUT:** −~150..250 (4:1 rq read and write-decode muxes, `pb[*][0][0]` root read mux, level-done
  compares, the `pushed` / room chain). The FF enables on oa_q/ob_q are free (CE pin).
- **Area-equivalent:** about −0.1 .. +0.2%, well inside the +1% allowance.
- **fmax:** the tree read path splits into:
  - `is_*` -> addr -> pb mux -> FF: about 3.2 ns of logic,
  - FF -> adder stage 1: about 2.5 ns.

  The 5.48 ns wall is gone. The next wall should be elsewhere; when NTB=2 broke the same wall, the
  design reached 112 MHz. Estimate **111-114 MHz (+3..6%)**, which gets accepted under the
  "fmax +3%, area <= +1%" rule and meets the 110 MHz target.

## Risks
- **The next critical path may sit just above 110 MHz.** Candidates are the `tr_go` priority /
  `tb_i[tr_b]` mux into `is_*`, `u_acc`'s `prev` mux, and the lane fmadd input muxes. Also, the
  est-fmax noise between runs (±2-4% seen in LESSONS) could hide the gain.
- **Off-by-one in the LT = LA+1 retiming** of `tr_v_q / tr_dst_q / tr_b_q / tr_r_q` or in
  `tb_inf` accounting would corrupt the sums. In particular, the root landing must use the same
  stage as the pb write. The bit-exact RSUM/RSSQ tests should catch it.
- **`tb_n` now reaches 0 while `tb_act` is still set.** `tr_go` must not issue then
  (`tb_i < tb_n` is false for 0 < 0, fine), and nothing else may treat `tb_n == 0` as a live level.
- **The one-entry `rq` relies on the invariant that `rq` drains every `ent` cycle it is non-empty.**
  If a future change gates the reduction write-out on something else, a deeper queue would be
  needed again. It would be worth an assertion (`!(rq_vld && push && !pop)`) under
  `ifndef SYNTHESIS`.
- **No references to otpu_fp internals** are added: only `otpu_fadd` ports are used, and no stage
  names appear in the code or comments.
implementation:
# Fold tree: registered pb operands, level advance at last issue, root pushed from the adder

Changes are all in `rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv`, following HYPOTHESIS.md:
- `g_tree`: `oa_q/ob_q` register the pb mux outputs on `ent` and feed `u_tree`. There is a new `LT = LA + 1`. The `tr_v_q/tr_dst_q/tr_b_q` delay lines are now `LT` deep, and a new `tr_r_q` root bit (`is_n == 1`) runs alongside them. The pb write-back and the `tb_inf` decrement use stage `LT-1`.
- A level now advances at its last issue: `tb_i + LANES >= tb_n` gives `tb_n >>= 1, tb_i = 0`. The level-done block is deleted. After the n = 1 level `tb_n` is 0, so `tb_i < tb_n` stops further issues while `tb_act` stays set until the root lands.
- The root goes into the queue straight from `tr_y[0]`, at the same stage as the pb write (the pb write still happens). `tb_act` is cleared in that cycle.
- `rq` is now a single entry (`rq_v, rq_a, rq_vld`). It is popped in every `ent` cycle it is valid (same `rows_done`/`fin` rules), and the push comes after the pop so it wins in the same cycle. `rq_h/rq_n`, the `pushed` chain and the room check are gone.
- I left out the suggested `!(rq_vld && push && !pop)` assertion. Push and pop sit in the same `ent` block and the pop is unconditional, so the assertion could never fire.
- `tb_inf` (3 bits) now peaks at 6 in-flight issues per buffer (6-cycle window from select to write), up from 5.
- Checks run: verilator lint is clean. These pass: `test_mlp_rtl[1]`, `test_attention_decode_rtl[1-8-2-100]`, `test_attention_layer_rtl[1]`, `test_fuzz_single_slice[0,1]`, `test_lane_count_does_not_change_results[4,16]`.
- Not measured: whether the cycle count matches HEAD exactly. The hypothesis argues it should (next level and root both still land in c7/c6), but the perf gates will be the first to confirm it.
lesson: Registering the fold-tree pb operands (LT=LA+1) and hiding the extra cycle by advancing the level at its last issue and pushing the root from the adder gave +2.4% fmax at +0.6% area, so no gain; the pb-mux/fadd path needs a deeper split.

title: Fold tree: stage the cross-lane operand in row 1 at write-back, so `ob` becomes a plain (buffer, row) read
hypothesis:
# Fold tree: stage the cross-lane operand in row 1 at write-back, so `ob` becomes a plain (buffer, row) read

Category: timing

## Motivation
The critical path (5.48 ns, 108 MHz) is the RSUM/RSSQ fold-tree operand read that feeds `u_tree`'s
first adder stage. It starts at `is_n[1]` and runs through an INV and carry `alu$39303` (the
`ia`/`ib` address arithmetic, 399→1144 ps). Then come about 8 LUT levels (1144→3538 ps, the
`pb[is_b][row][k]` / `pb[is_b][0][lane]` operand muxes plus ftz), and last the adder's
magnitude compare/swap and exponent subtract (3538→5480 ps).

The operand mux in front of the adder is wider than it needs to be:
- `ob` is two muxes plus a 2:1 mode select. One is a 4-buffer × 8-row mux (levels n >= LANES). The
  other is a 4-buffer × 8-lane cross-lane mux on row 0 (levels n < LANES, lane `(is_i+k+is_n)[2:0]`).
  Both selects come out of 7-bit adders on `is_i`/`is_n`. That is a 64:1 mux behind an adder, per bit, per lane.
- `oa` is a 4 × 8 = 32:1 mux, but only rows 0..3 can hold a valid `oa` (ia < n <= 32).

Earlier rounds only nibbled at this. Registering the binary row selects gave +1.5%, and pruning the
lane candidates with extra select logic gave +2.9% fmax at +2.6% area. The cross-lane leg survived
both. NTB=2 halved this mux and reached 112 MHz, so this mux really is the limit, but NTB=2 is ruled
out by the perf gate. This proposal removes the cross-lane leg entirely at zero latency cost.

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)
1. **Write-back staging of the next level's `ob` into row 1.** In levels n <= LANES (8, 4, 2 for
   LANES=8), the next level (n/2) needs lane `k + n/2` of row 0 as tree adder k's `ob`. When a
   level-n result comes back, adder `k + n/2`'s result is `x[k + n/2]` of the next level. For
   k < n/2, also write that result into `pb[b][1][k]`:
   ```
   for h = 1, 2, .., LANES/2:  if (tr_n_q[LA-1] == 2h)
     for k < h: if (tr_v_q[LA-1][k+h]) pb[tr_b_q[LA-1]][1][k] <= tr_y[k+h];
   ```
   Add `tr_n_q[LA]` (7 b) to the tree pipe next to `tr_dst_q`/`tr_b_q` (`tr_n_q[0] <= is_n`).
   The normal write-back (`pb[b][dst>>LW][k] <= tr_y[k]`) is unchanged, so row 0 still holds
   x[0..LANES-1] and the root `pb[bb][0][0]` is unchanged.
2. **Read side:**
   - `ob = pb[is_b][is_rb][k]`, where `is_rb` is registered at selection time:
     `is_rb <= (tb_n[tr_b] >= LANES) ? 3'((tb_i[tr_b] + tb_n[tr_b]) >> LW) : 3'd1`. That is a
     4 × 8 mux driven straight from FFs, with no lane leg and no adder.
   - `oa = pb[is_b][is_i[OAW+LW-1:LW]][k]`, with `OAW = $clog2(RL/2)` (2 bits for LANES=8). This
     is a 4 × 4 mux read from FFs (`is_i` is a multiple of LANES, so `(is_i+k)>>LW == is_i>>LW`).
   - `tr_m` (`ia < is_n`) stays as it is. It only feeds `tr_v_q`.

### Why results stay bit-identical
- Each add sees exactly the same operand pair as before, and adds run in the same order and on the
  same cycles.
- Row 1 is dead from level LANES down: level LANES reads it as `ob` at issue, and the next level issues only after
  `tb_inf == 0`, i.e. after all write-backs. Each extra write lands only after that level's reads
  of row 1 are done, and before the next level issues.
- The normal write-backs of levels n <= LANES all go to row 0, so they never collide with the row-1 extras.
- The buffer being captured into is never tree-active (the existing `stall` rule), and extras only target `tr_b_q`.
- `oa`/`ob` values on invalid lanes (ia >= n) change, but they were don't-care before and still
  are, because `tr_v_q` masks them.
- `oa` rows >= RL/2 are never valid for a live pair (is_i < tb_n <= 32).
- No latency, handshake or perf change: the cycle-by-cycle schedule is identical.

## Expected
- fmax: the tree-read path loses the address carry (~0.75 ns) and 1–2 mux levels, dropping to
  roughly 4.4–4.7 ns. The next-worst path then limits. NTB=2 + registered rows (a comparable mux
  width) reached 112 MHz, so expect about 111–113 MHz (+3–5%), which meets the 110 MHz target.
- LUT: the cross-lane `ob` leg is removed (8 lanes × 32 b × a 4×8 mux + 2:1 mode mux) and the `oa`
  rows are halved. Adding the row-1 write-data 4:1 select (4 lanes × 32 b, shared by the buffers)
  gives an estimated −1000 to −2500 LUTs.
- FF: +31 (tr_n_q) + 3 (is_rb).
- Area-eq: −2% to −4%.

## Risks
- If Yosys had already collapsed the lane mux, the LUT savings shrink. Timing still gains from
  dropping the adder in front of the select.
- The next-worst path (unknown: lane fmadd operand mux, capture write decode, RMAX) may sit just
  above 5.3 ns and cap the fmax gain below +3%. Area should still drop, via the −1% criterion,
  but only if fmax >= 110 MHz.
- Correctness hinges on the row-1 staging invariant for general LANES. It needs RL >= 2 (always
  true for LANES <= 16) and the level-n normal write-back going to row 0 for n <= LANES (true,
  since tb_i = 0 there). The tests check this bit-exactly.
- The row-1 D-input gets another source, a slightly deeper mux on `pb[*][1][0..LANES/2-1]`. That
  path runs from the `tr_y` register, which is short.
implementation:
# Fold tree: row-1 staging of the cross-lane operand (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv)

- Tree read side: `ob = pb[is_b][is_rb][k]` and `oa = pb[is_b][is_i[OAW+LW-1:LW]][k]`. The cross-lane leg, the `ib` adder and the `is_n >= LANES` mode mux are gone. `ia` stays, but it only feeds `tr_m`.
- `is_rb` (RW = $clog2(RL) bits) is registered next to `is_i`/`is_n` at selection time: `(tb_i + tb_n) >> LW` for n >= LANES, else 1.
- The write-back pipe carries `tr_n_q[LA]` (the level's n). For levels n = 2h <= LANES, the write-back also stores `tr_y[k+h]` into `pb[b][1][k]` for k < h, gated by `tr_v_q[k+h]`. The loop runs over j < LW with h = 1 << j. The normal row-0 write-back and the root read are unchanged.
- Updated the pb-layout comment and added localparams `RW` and `OAW`. No port, handshake or schedule changes.
- Checks: Verilator lint is clean for otpu_vpu. `test_mlp_rtl[1]` passes, and `-k "lane_count or attention_layer"` passes 4/4 (lane-count covers LANES = 4 and 16).
- Reviewer: this relies on row 1 being dead from level LANES on. Level LANES reads row 1 in its single issue cycle, before any of its write-backs. For LANES = 1 there is no staging; level 1 reads row 1 through `is_rb` = (0+1) >> 0.
lesson: Fold-tree write-back staging of cross-lane ob into row 1 (4×8 ob / 4×4 oa mux from FFs, no adders) gave only +2.4% fmax, −0.7% area; the operand mux alone isn't enough, so pair it with an adder-side cut.

title: Fold tree: index `pb` with the bits a live tree pair can actually use (tree writes only rows < RL/2)
hypothesis:
# Fold tree: index `pb` with the bits a live tree pair can actually use (tree writes only rows < RL/2)

Category: area

## Motivation

The fold buffers `pb[NTB=4][RL=8][LANES=8]` are 8192 FFs. In the current RTL, every one of those
FFs has two write sources:

- capture: `pb[cap_sel][mt.sub[5:0]][l] <= pacc[l]` (line 732)
- tree write-back: `pb[tr_b_q[LA-1]][tr_dst_q[LA-1][5:0] >> LW][k] <= tr_y[k]` (line 761)

After `memory_map`/`opt_dff`, each bit therefore gets `D = tree_we ? tr_y : pacc` plus CE, which
costs about one LUT per bit, so roughly 8192 LUTs of the champion's 42944.

The tree can never write rows 4..7:

- Level n reads `x[i]` and `x[i+n]` and writes only `x[i]`, for `i < n <= NP/2 = 32`.
- The write row is `is_i >> LW`, where `is_i = tb_i` is a multiple of LANES and `is_i < is_n <= 32`
  whenever any lane of the issue is live (`tr_v_q != 0`). So `is_i[6:5] == 0` and the row is below
  `32/LANES = RL/2 = 4`.

Yosys has no way to know this, because `tb_i` and `is_i` are 7-bit registers. Its write decoder
therefore builds tree-write enables and a D mux for all 8 rows. Half of that mux, 4 buffers × 4
rows × 8 lanes × 32 b = 4096 bits, is dead logic.

The read side follows the same invariant:

- `oa = pb[is_b][ia[5:0] >> LW][k]` is a 32:1 word mux behind a 7-bit adder (`ia = is_i + k`), but
  a live `oa` only ever reads rows `is_i[4:LW]` (0..3). That makes it a 16:1 mux with no adder.
- `ob` for n >= LANES goes through two chained adders (`ib = is_i + k + is_n`). Because `is_i` is a
  multiple of LANES below the power of two `is_n`, `(is_i + k + is_n) >> LW == (is_i | is_n) >> LW`,
  so ob needs no carry at all.

The critical path starts at `is_n[1]` and runs through exactly that `ib` carry (alu$39303 at
526→1144 ps) and then about 9 LUT levels of pb mux before the tree fadd. So the read part also
takes one carry chain and roughly one mux level off the 5.48 ns path.

## Change

All edits are in `rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv`, in the RSUM/RSSQ fold tree only.

1. Add a width for the tree-reachable row index (1 bit for LANES=16):
   ```systemverilog
   localparam int TRW = $clog2(NP / 2);          // live tree pair indices are < NP/2
   ```

2. Tree write-back (line 761). Change the row index to use only bits a live write can have:
   ```systemverilog
   if (tr_v_q[LA-1][k]) pb[tr_b_q[LA-1]][tr_dst_q[LA-1][TRW-1:LW]][k] <= tr_y[k];
   ```
   The index is now a (TRW-LW)-bit value, so rows RL/2..RL-1 get no tree-write port. Their FFs
   become `D = pacc[l]` with CE = capture decode, which removes the LUT per bit.

   Optional: narrow `tr_dst_q` to `[TRW-1:LW]` as well. That saves a few FFs and is not required.

3. Tree reads (`g_tree`, lines ~558-566). Drop the `ia`/`ib` adders from the operand address and
   keep them only for `tr_m`:
   ```systemverilog
   logic [6:0] ia;
   assign ia = is_i + 7'(k);
   assign tr_m[k] = is_go && (ia < is_n);
   logic [LW-1:0] lb;                             // n < LANES: lane k + n of row 0
   assign lb = LW'(k) + is_n[LW-1:0];
   assign oa = pb[is_b][is_i[TRW-1:LW]][k];
   assign ob = (is_n >= 7'(LANES)) ? pb[is_b][(is_i[5:LW] | is_n[5:LW])][k]
                                   : pb[is_b][0][lb];
   ```
   The `ob` row expression has width 6-LW = log2(RL) bits.

   Do not replicate candidate muxes per buffer, and do not restructure the n < LANES leg. That is
   what made r20260924-025910-s1 and r20260924-030642-s0 grow.

Nothing else changes: no latencies, no control, no `tb_*` logic, and no capture path.

### Why the results stay bit-identical

- `tb_n` is set to NP/2 at capture and only ever halved. `tb_i` is reset to 0 and only incremented
  by LANES. So `is_i` is always a multiple of LANES, and `is_i < is_n <= NP/2` whenever the issue
  has a live lane.
- For levels n < LANES, the level issues only once, with `is_i = 0`.

Given those facts, check each lane with `tr_m[k] = 1`:

- **oa:** `ia >> LW = (is_i + k) >> LW = is_i >> LW` because k < LANES and `is_i[LW-1:0] = 0`. Its
  bits above TRW-1 are 0, so `is_i[TRW-1:LW]` addresses the same word.
- **ob, n >= LANES:** `is_i + is_n = is_i | is_n` because `is_n` is a power of two and `is_i < is_n`,
  so `is_i` has no bit at or above `is_n`'s. Adding k causes no carry into bit LW, because
  `is_i[LW-1:0] = 0`. So
  `ib >> LW = (is_i | is_n) >> LW`, which is below RL.
- **ob, n < LANES:** `ib[LW-1:0] = (0 + k + is_n)[LW-1:0] = lb`.
- **Write-back:** `tr_dst_q = is_i` of a live issue is below NP/2, so the truncated index names the
  same row.

For lanes with `tr_m[k] = 0`, the fadd output is never written (`tr_v_q` gates the write), so
reading a different word there changes nothing. The otpu_fadd pipeline carries no state between
issues. Capture writes, tree ordering, fp rounding and the root read `pb[bb][0][0]` are untouched.

## Expected

**Area**

| Item | LUT effect |
|---|---|
| Write-back D-mux for rows 4..7 | about −4000 (4096 bit-muxes + row decode) |
| Row decode for the removed tree-write ports | small extra saving |
| oa 32:1 → 16:1, with two 7-bit adders per lane removed | about −800 to −1000 |
| ob adders removed | about −100 |

- Total: roughly −4500 to −5000 LUTs, so 42944 → about 38000–38500.
- FFs: unchanged (a few fewer if `tr_dst_q` is narrowed). DSP and LUT-RAM: unchanged.
- Area-equivalent: 59746 → about 54800–55300, which is **−7% to −8%**, far past the 1% bar.

**fmax**

- The critical path loses the `is_n → ib` carry (about 0.6 ns in the report) and one oa mux level.
- Precomputing addresses alone gave +1.5% (r20260924-014914-s0), and the read-side invariant
  pruning gave +2.9% (r20260924-025910-s1).
- Expect about 108 → 110–111 MHz, which would reach the 110 target together with the large area
  drop.

## Risks

- **fmax may miss 110.** The area win is robust, but acceptance also needs est fmax >= 110. If ABC
  reshuffles and the pb/fadd path stays at about 5.45 ns, the result is no_gain on fmax despite
  −7% area. Only the read-side part (step 3) aims at timing; step 2 is timing-neutral.
- **Width or lint mistakes.** `is_i[5:LW] | is_n[5:LW]` must be exactly log2(RL) bits. For
  LANES=8 the three indices are `[4:3]`, `[5:3]` and a 3-bit lb. Verilator will flag width
  mismatches.
- **Yosys memory inference.** If Yosys keeps `pb` as a `$mem` with a full-width write port instead
  of constant-folding the upper row bits, the saving shrinks. The narrowed index is a genuinely
  narrower address, so `memory_map` should not generate words 4..7 for that port.
- **No functional or protocol risk** as long as the invariants above hold. They follow directly from
  the `tb_n` / `tb_i` update rules, which this change does not touch. The RSUM/RSSQ bit-exact tests
  cover all levels (n = 32 .. 1) and all four buffers.

# Fixed end taps for the composite results (kill the false `fp_max -> st[wtap] -> EXP2 adder` path) + fold-tree ob staging

Category: timing

## Motivation

Two separate paths sit above the 110 MHz line (5.37 ns logic for 110, 5.31 ns for +3% = 111.1 MHz;
est fmax = 1000 / (1.6 * ns + 0.5)).

1. **Fold-tree read, 5.48 ns (champion).** Starts at `is_n` and goes through the `ib = ia + is_n`
   carry, the `pb` operand muxes and the tree adder's first stage. Eight attempts cut it, but
   the best ones only reached +2.4%. The reason is the second path.

2. **The lanes' result mux, 5.35 to 5.39 ns: the path that caps every tree fix.** The saved
   reports of the no-gain runs show it:
   - `build/tourney/otpu_vpu/r20260924-030642-s1/.../sta.txt` and `r20260924-031822-s0`:
     5347 ps, both +2.4% (110.4 MHz).
   - `r20260924-014914-s0`: 5392 ps, endpoint literally `\lres[223]`, i.e. lane 1 (a long lane)
     bit 31.

   The path is the same in all three:
   `m0[85]` (= `m0.bmode[1]`) -> `y` mux -> `fp_max/fp_min` compare (CARRY4 x3) -> `st[0].v`
   -> a chain of 5 LUT3/LUT4 (the priority mux `t = st[wtap]` over the 11 boundaries) -> CARRY4 x2-3
   (`t.v + {t.ii, 23'd0}`, the EXP2 exponent add) -> `lres` -> `cw_data` -> `tw_data`.

   **This is a false path.** `st[0].v` is only the result of a 0-slot function (MAX/MIN/COPY/ABS/FILL).
   The EXP2 adder only ever sees `st[9]`, because an EXP2 entry is only selected when
   `wtap == n_slots(V_EXP2) == 9`. Synthesis cannot know that, so it builds the full
   `11-way mux -> adder` cone for every tap. It costs about 0.35 ns of LUT chain plus about
   0.45 ns of carry on the critical path, and about 76 live bits x 11:1 mux per long lane.

   Removing path 2 alone does nothing (path 1 stays at 5.48). Fixing path 1 alone gives +2.4%
   (path 2 takes over). **Both must go together.** The next wall after both is the RSUM/RSSQ
   squarer's DSP cascade (`xa -> ftz/mask -> u_sq DSP A -> PCOUT -> PCIN`) at 5.279 ns,
   measured in `r20260924-014914-s1`. That gives about 111.8 MHz (+3.6%).

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)

### Part A: fixed end taps in the long lanes' result mux (`g_lane`, the "result of the entry that ends at a tap" block)

Replace

```systemverilog
    always_comb begin
      lst_t t;
      t = st[wtap];
      case (mo.func)
        V_EXP2, V_EXP2SUB:
          lres[l] = t.f[0] ? F_ZERO : t.f[1] ? F_INF : (t.v + {t.ii, 23'd0});
        V_RECIP:
          lres[l] = t.f[0] ? F_ZERO : t.f[1] ? {t.f[2], 31'd0} : (t.f[2] ? fneg(t.k2) : t.k2);
        V_RSQRT:
          lres[l] = t.f[0] ? F_ZERO : t.k2;
        default:
          lres[l] = t.v;
      endcase
    end
```

with

```systemverilog
    // the result of the entry that ends at a tap this cycle: a function only ends at its own
    // last slot (wtap == n_slots(mo.func)), so each composite reads its fixed tap and only the
    // 0/1-slot functions select by wtap
    localparam int TE = n_slots(V_EXP2), TR = n_slots(V_RECIP), TQ = n_slots(V_RSQRT);
    always_comb begin
      case (mo.func)
        V_EXP2, V_EXP2SUB:
          lres[l] = st[TE].f[0] ? F_ZERO : st[TE].f[1] ? F_INF : (st[TE].v + {st[TE].ii, 23'd0});
        V_RECIP:
          lres[l] = st[TR].f[0] ? F_ZERO : st[TR].f[1] ? {st[TR].f[2], 31'd0} :
                    (st[TR].f[2] ? fneg(st[TR].k2) : st[TR].k2);
        V_RSQRT:
          lres[l] = st[TQ].f[0] ? F_ZERO : st[TQ].k2;
        default:
          lres[l] = (wtap == 0) ? st[0].v : st[1].v;
      endcase
    end
```

If a tool rejects the constant-function call in the localparam, use the literals 9, 6 and 10.
Keep `wtap`/`mo` as they are, since `mo` still drives `cw_*`. The short lanes are unchanged: they
already use `(wtap == 0) ? st[0] : st[1]`.

**Why the results are bit-identical.**
- `mo`/`wtap` come from the same priority loop, and it only selects an entry with
  `n_slots(mtap[s].func) == s`. So whenever `mo.v`:
  - EXP2/EXP2SUB means `wtap == 9`;
  - RECIP means 6;
  - RSQRT means 10;
  - the other elementwise functions mean 0 or 1.
- The old code read `st[wtap]`, which in each case is exactly the tap now hard-wired.
- When `!mo.v`, `lres` is not used: `cw_*` only takes `lres` under `mo.v && mask`, and the RMAX
  and RSUM lane-0 overrides don't read it.
- The expressions and the fp rounding are the same; only the source mux changes. No latency or
  protocol change.

### Part B: fold-tree second operand staged into row 1 (exactly the r20260924-031822-s0 patch, which passed all gates)

Apply `tools/tourney/runs/otpu_vpu/patches/r20260924-031822-s0.patch`. It was made against blob
`a71d96a`, which is the current file, so it applies cleanly. In short:
- Add `localparam int RW = $clog2(RL), OAW = $clog2(RL / 2);`, `logic [RW-1:0] is_rb;` and a
  `tr_n_q [LA]` pipe next to `tr_dst_q`.
- In `g_tree`, drop `ib`:
  `oa = pb[is_b][is_i[OAW+LW-1:LW]][k]; ob = pb[is_b][is_rb][k];`.
  There are no adders or cross-lane mux in front of the tree fadd, and every adder reads the
  same (buffer, row), since `is_i` is a multiple of LANES.
- At selection:
  `is_rb <= (tb_n[tr_b] >= LANES) ? RW'((tb_i[tr_b] + tb_n[tr_b]) >> LW) : RW'(1);`
- At write-back, for levels `n = 2h <= LANES` (`tr_n_q[LA-1] == 2 << j`, `j < LW`), also write
  `tr_y[k + h]` into `pb[buf][1][k]` for `k < h`. Row 1 is dead from level LANES on (level n =
  LANES issues all its pairs in one cycle, so it reads row 1 before any staging lands). This
  makes lane k of row 1 hold exactly `x[k + n]` for the next level.
- The same adds are done in the same order with the same operands, so the fold is bit-identical.
  Tree latency per level is unchanged. It passed the full fast, board and perf gates in
  r20260924-031822-s0 (LANES 4/8/16 included).

## Expected

- **Part B alone (measured):** area -0.7%; tree path ≤ 5.347 ns (the lres path was the critical
  one in that run).
- **Part A:** the `fp_max -> lres` path falls to about 3.9-4.1 ns: `fp_max` select at about 3.47 ns,
  then about 2 LUTs to `tw_data`. The 11:1 × ~76-bit `st[wtap]` mux in each of the 2 long lanes
  becomes a 2 to 3 input mux per field. Estimated -300 to -500 LUTs (about -0.5 to -0.8% area-eq).
  FF unchanged.
- **Combined:** area-eq about 59,000 (-1.2% to -1.5%). The critical path becomes the u_sq DSP
  cascade at about 5.28 ns, giving **about 111.8 MHz (+3.6%)**. The worst case, if the staged
  tree read lands just under its measured bound, is 5.347 ns = 110.4 MHz. That still meets the
  target, with area ≤ -1%. So either acceptance rule should hold.
- **Perf:** unchanged. There is no latency change anywhere.

## Risks

- The tree path in the staged design was only bounded (≤ 5.347 ns), not measured. If it sits at
  5.32-5.35, fmax is +2.4-2.9%, and the change relies on area ≤ -1%. That hinges on Part A saving
  ≥ 0.3%. It very likely does, since it removes two ~76-bit 11:1 muxes.
- Part A depends on the invariant `wtap == n_slots(mo.func)` whenever `mo.v`. It holds by
  construction of the `wtap` loop. Any future function whose last slot differs from its
  `n_slots` would break it, so the comment says so.
- Constant-function localparam: some tools choke. Literals are the fallback.
- Synthesis noise: abc9 has moved the lres path between 5.25 and 5.39 ns across runs, so the
  new critical path could land ±0.05 ns from the estimate.

# RSUM/RSSQ: streaming fold tree (delay lines + fixed slot schedule) replaces the pb buffers

Category: structure

## Motivation

Every recent round attacked the same 5.48 ns wall (`is_n` -> `ib = ia + is_n` carry -> ~9 LUT
levels of `pb[is_b][row][lane]` read mux -> fp_add_s1 compare/exp-diff carry chains -> FF) and
kept the `pb[NTB][RL][LANES]` fold buffers. Registering selects gave +1.5%, pruning/replicating
the mux +2.4..2.9%, extra latency failed the attention_decode perf gate, and NTB 4->2 broke timing
(112 MHz) but also broke perf. The buffers are also the largest block in the unit:
`pb` = 4 x 8 x 8 x 32 = **8192 FFs** (35% of the 23574 FF), each with a capture-or-tree-result D mux
and write decode, plus the two 32:1 / ~60:1 read muxes on all 8 lanes x 32 bits (the logic on the
critical path). Moving `pb` to LUT-RAM alone saved 15% area, which shows how much sits there.

The buffers are not needed. The final partials of a row arrive **in order, one row of LANES
partials per stream cycle**: sub s = 0..RL-1 on consecutive `en` cycles (the last RL chunks of
the row are issued back to back). isum_64's folding tree (`n = 32,16,..,1: x[i] = x[i] + x[i+n]`,
opentpu/fp32.py `interleaved_sum`) pairs row r with row r+H at level H = RL/2, RL/4, .., 1. Those
are fixed distances in time, so a streaming tree with **delay lines** does the same adds.
Row starts are always a multiple of RL `en` cycles apart (nch is padded to a multiple of RL, rows
are issued back to back, and a reduction runs alone). So a fixed schedule modulo RL can share
LANES adders across all row levels with no conflicts, and nothing ever needs to stall.

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)

Remove: `pb`, `tb_act/tb_n/tb_i/tb_inf/tb_dst`, `cap_sel`, `tr_go/tr_b`, `is_go/is_b/is_i/is_n`,
`tr_m`, `tr_dst_q/tr_b_q/tr_v_q`, the `rq_*` queue, and `stall` (so `en = gnt`; `ent` = `en`).
The `pb` capture and the whole tree/level/push block in the sequencer go too.

Add the following. Times are in `en` cycles, relative to A = the cycle the row's sub-0 final
partial is on `pacc` (with `cap = red_act && is_sum && live(mt, tag) && mt.final_`):

1. **Row levels on the existing LANES tree adders `u_tree` (en).** Level j = 0..LR-1
   (LR = log2 RL) has H_j = RL >> (j+1) pairs. Pair r of level j issues at A + I_j + r:
   * I_0 = H_0 (the pair's b operand, row r+H_0, is on `pacc` right then);
   * I_j = I_{j-1} - H_j + RL * ceil((LA + 2*H_j) / RL)  (constant function).
   So level j always issues in residues [H_j, 2H_j) mod RL. These residue sets are disjoint
   (residue 0 is free), and two rows are a multiple of RL apart. So two issues can only
   collide if they are the same level, the same pair and the same row: the adders are never
   double-booked. It also satisfies I_j >= I_{j-1} + LA + H_j, so both operands have landed.
   LANES = 8 (RL = 8, LA = 4): I = 4, 10, 17 -> residues {4..7}, {2,3}, {1}.
2. **Operands** (the ISA order is kept: a = x[i], b = x[i+n]):
   * level 0: a = `pacc[k]` delayed H_0 (`otpu_delay`, N = H_0, SRL-friendly), b = `pacc[k]`;
   * level j >= 1: a = `tr_y[k]` delayed Da_j = I_j - I_{j-1} - LA, b = `tr_y[k]` delayed
     Db_j = Da_j - H_j. These are taps of one FF chain `tyd[0..DMAX]` on `tr_y` (LANES = 8:
     Da/Db = 2/0 and 3/2, so DMAX = 3, 768 FFs).
   Each adder input is a mux of LR registered sources, selected by registered one-hot level
   strobes. **Level 0 is the default** (when no level >= 1 strobe is set), so the select never
   waits on the `cap` decode. The path is FF -> 1 LUT -> fp_add_s1 instead of FF -> adder ->
   9 LUTs -> fp_add_s1. A non-issuing cycle just feeds the adder values that nothing reads.
3. **Strobes / valids** are resettable shift registers on `en` (no power-up garbage):
   v_j = (cap && sub >= RL - H_j) delayed by Δ_j = I_j - (RL - H_j) (LANES = 8: Δ = 0, 4, 10).
   The last level and the root share one shift register fed by `cap && mt.row_last`
   (row_last is sub RL-1).
4. **Cross-lane levels (n < LANES): a dedicated pipeline of LANES-1 `otpu_fadd` (en)**, with
   no muxes and no control. Level m = LANES/2..1: `y_m[k] = fadd(y_2m[k], y_2m[k+m])` for
   k < m, where y_LANES = `tr_y` (valid at A + I_{LR-1} + LA). The root `y_1[0]` is valid at
   A + I_{LR-1} + LA*(1 + log2 LANES), which is a tap of the row_last shift register
   (LANES = 8: 26 cycles after row_last).
5. **Write-back:** `if (red_act && is_sum && root_v) cw_en[0], cw_addr[0] = wr_row,
   cw_data[0] = y_1[0]`. `wr_row` is set to dst at begin and advanced by `drs` per root
   (rows finish in order), which replaces `tb_dst/rq_a`. On `root_v && en`: rows_done++, and
   `fin` when it reaches `rows`. At most one root per RL cycles and reductions run alone, so
   nothing else can collide with it: no queue is needed. While gnt is low everything
   (including root_v) is frozen, so the write is registered exactly once, like the `mo`
   elementwise writes.
6. Header comment: replace the "two buffers / folding tree" text with the streaming
   description.

Generic in LANES (the tests use 4, 8 and 16): LANES = 4 -> RL 16, levels 8,4,2,1, I = 8, 20, 34,
49 (checked: residues {8..15}, {4..7}, {2,3}, {1}); LANES = 16 -> RL 4, levels 2,1,
I = 2, 9 (residues {2,3}, {1}). For LANES = 16, ceil((4 + 2)/4) = 2.

**Why the results are bit-identical:** every add is `fp_add(x[i], x[i+n])` on the same two values
and in the same operand order as `interleaved_sum`. Only when each add happens changes. The partial
loop (`u_sq/u_acc/u_fb`), RMAX and the elementwise lanes are untouched.

## Expected

* Removed: 8192 pb FFs + their D-mux/CE LUTs (about 4-8k LUT), the oa/ob read muxes (about 7k LUT),
  rq (256 FF), tree control (about 200 LUT), and the stall term on every `en` CE.
* Added: 7 fadds (about 350 LUT + 190 FF each: +2.5k LUT, +1.3k FF), tyd chain 768 FF, pacc delay
  (256 SRL + 256 FF), 2 x 256 mux LUTs, about 60 control FFs.
* Net: **LUT about -8k to -12k, FF about -6.5k, area-eq about -10% to -18%** (the LUT-RAM `pb`
  alone was -15%).
* fmax: the 5.48 ns tree-read wall is gone. The new tree operand path looks like `u_acc`'s
  (FF -> 1 LUT -> fp_add_s1). When this wall broke before (NTB = 2), the design reached 112 MHz,
  so expect **>= 110 MHz**, and the simpler `en` helps too.
* Perf: better, not worse. There are no stalls (the current design needs >= 10 issue cycles per
  row and stalls on 64-column rows), and the root arrives 26 cycles after the row's last
  partial instead of about 40. So attention_decode and the Qwen3 proxy should speed up.

## Risks

* Schedule arithmetic: an off-by-one in I_j, Da/Db or Δ silently pairs the wrong rows. The RTL
  tests catch it (bit-exact), but check the LANES = 4 and 16 cases too
  (test_lane_count_does_not_change_results).
* Yosys/Verilator constant functions: keep them simple (an int loop over j), or unroll per level
  in a generate loop with localparams.
* The assumption that rows are a multiple of RL `en` cycles apart must hold. It depends on nch
  padding, back-to-back row issue, reductions running alone and stall = 0. If a future change
  inserts a bubble, rows would collide. Could add a `$fatal`/assert in simulation that no two
  level strobes fire together.
* The seven new fadds could create a new near-critical path if the placer spreads them. They are
  pure FF-to-FF pipelines, so this is unlikely.
* If area comes in lower than expected, the next step is to fold the cross-lane levels onto 5
  time-multiplexed adders (LANES = 8 only). That is not part of this change.
implementation:
# RSUM/RSSQ streaming fold tree (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv)

- Removed `pb`, the `tb_*`/`cap_sel`/`tr_go`/`is_*`/`tr_m`/`tr_*_q` tree control, the `rq_*` queue, `stall` and `ent`. `en = gnt` now drives everything, and ta/tb_en and the elementwise write no longer have stall gating.
- Row levels (j = 0..LR-1, H = RL>>(j+1)) are scheduled with constant functions `tree_h/tree_i/tree_da/tree_db/tree_dmax`, following the I_j recurrence in HYPOTHESIS.md (LANES=8: I = 4,10,17; Da/Db = 2/0, 3/2; DMAX = 3; DL = 10; RD = 26).
- In each lane of `g_tree`, `u_tree` takes level 0 operands from `pacc` delayed H_0 (`u_pd`, `otpu_delay`) and `pacc`. Level j >= 1 operands come from taps of the `td` FF chain on `tr_y`. Registered strobes `lv[j]` select the level; level 0 is the default.
- Strobes are resettable shift registers on `en`. Each middle level has its own register (`g_lv`), fed by `cap && sub >= RL-H`. The last level and the root share `rsr`, fed by `cap && row_last`: `lv[LR-1] = rsr[DL-1]` and `root_v = rsr[RD-1]`.
- The cross-lane levels use a dedicated pipeline of LANES-1 `otpu_fadd`s (`g_xl`, array `xl`); the root is `xl[LW][0]`. On `root_v`, the root is written to `wr_row`. `wr_row` is set to dst at the start and advanced by `drs` per root; `rows_done`/`fin` work as before.
- Added a sim-only `$fatal` in the existing `ifndef SYNTHESIS` block: it fires if level 0 (cap of sub >= RL/2) ever coincides with a level strobe, which would mean rows are not RL-aligned.
- Checked: verilator lint is clean; test_mlp_rtl[1], test_lane_count_does_not_change_results[4,16], test_attention_decode_rtl[1-8-2-100], test_scoreboard_stress_single_slice[0] and test_fuzz_single_slice[0] pass.
- Reviewer note: correctness depends on rows being exactly a multiple of RL `en` cycles apart (nch padding, back-to-back issue, reductions alone). Any future bubble in the reduction stream would break the schedule (the sim assert above should catch it).
lesson: RSUM/RSSQ streaming fold tree (delay lines + fixed mod-RL slot schedule, no stall) replacing the 8192-FF pb buffers: area -20.8%, fmax only +1.2% (109 MHz). The area win is real, but the critical path is elsewhere.

title: Take the SRL clock-to-out off every fadd input: real last-stage FFs for u_fb / u_pd / fmadd c
hypothesis:
# Take the SRL clock-to-out off every fadd input: real last-stage FFs for u_fb / u_pd / fmadd c

Category: timing

## Motivation

The critical path (5.412 ns) starts at an **SRL16E**:

    1568  SRL16E.CLK->Q      -> \g_red[7].u_fb.g_regs.qr[27]
    1975  LUT5               (prev = mtq.first ? 0 : fb)
    ...   6 LUT levels + 2 CARRY4 chains   (fp_add_s1 in u_acc: ftz, 31-bit compare, swap, exp diff)
    5412  FDRE.D             (u_acc s1 register)

`qr` is supposed to be a plain flip-flop. otpu_delay marks its last stage
`(* shreg_extract = "no", keep *)` for exactly this reason ("an SRL's clock-to-out is ~1.5 ns"),
but Yosys `shregmap -tech xilinx` ignores both attributes. It packs the whole chain
`r[0..N-2], qr` into one SRL16E, and `qr` becomes the SRL's output net. So 1.47 ns of the
5.41 ns is SRL clk->Q (an FDRE's clk->Q is about 0.3 ns). Another 0.41 ns is the `first` mux
in front of the adder.

The same pattern feeds other fp_add_s1 stages in this file:
* `u_tree` operand a: `pd` comes from `u_pd` (otpu_delay N = RL/2 = 4, so an SRL). It goes through the
  LUT5 oa mux into fp_add_s1. That's the same depth as the reported path (8 adders).
* The lane fmadds' c operand: `rc` -> `u_ma.u_c` (N = LM = 2) forms a 3-FF chain with no taps
  (`rc`, `r[0]`, `qr`). That reaches the minlen-3 of shregmap, so `cd` probably also comes out of an
  SRL16E into fp_add_s1 (26 fmadds).

The histogram agrees: about 400 endpoints sit in (5149, 5420], and 16–42 adders each have
around 10 deep s1 endpoints (the d / compare-dependent bits). Earlier rounds kept cutting the pb
mux, the operand selects and the tree schedule for 1–3% each. That work missed this cause, which is the SRL
clock-to-out on the adder inputs. Several lessons point at it without naming it: "the fmadd's
prev/ic_ mux leg", "pb in LUT-RAM ... RAM read sits in the issue cycle", "RSUM/RSSQ fold tree:
critical path is elsewhere".

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)

Stop shregmap from absorbing the last stage. shregmap only packs `$dff`/`$dffe` without reset
(it runs after `simplemap t:$dff t:$dffe`, `-minlen 3`). So in each case the last stage either becomes a
sync-reset FF or ends up in a chain shorter than 3.

### (a) Partial loop `u_fb`: fold the `first` clear into a registered `prev`

```systemverilog
// mtq.first one granted cycle early (mtq = m0r delayed LM)
logic first_e;
otpu_delay #(.W(1), .N(LM - 1)) u_fe (.clk, .en, .d(m0.first), .q(first_e));
...
for (genvar l ...) begin : g_red
  f32_t xin, tq, prev, fbm;
  ...
  if (RL > LA) begin : g_fbq
    // pacc delayed RL-LA-1, then a clearing register: its sync clear keeps it out of the SRL,
    // so the adder sees a flip-flop, not a shift-register LUT's 1.5 ns clock-to-out
    otpu_delay #(.W(32), .N(RL - LA - 1)) u_fb (.clk, .en, .d(pacc[l]), .q(fbm));
    always_ff @(posedge clk) if (en) prev <= first_e ? F_ZERO : fbm;
  end else begin : g_fbw
    assign fbm = pacc[l];
    assign prev = mtq.first ? F_ZERO : pacc[l];
  end
  otpu_fadd #(.LAT(LA)) u_acc (.clk, .en, .a(prev), .b(tq), .y(pacc[l]));
end
```
Bit-identical, counting granted cycles k (every register involved advances on `en`):
old `prev[k] = mtq.first[k] ? 0 : pacc[k-(RL-LA)]`. New:
`prev[k] = first_e[k-1] ? 0 : fbm[k-1] = m0.first[k-LM] ? 0 : pacc[k-1-(RL-LA-1)]`, which is
the same because `mtq.first[k] = m0.first[k-LM]`. `first_e` is also bit 0 of u_mtq's first stage, so
opt_merge may share it. The clear maps to a sync reset (or CE-gated R on one shared LUT), so
the per-bit LUT5 mux disappears and the SRL (now 3 deep) feeds an FF.

### (b) Tree level 0 `u_pd`: reuse the loop line (LANES = 8: RL/2 == RL-LA == 4)

```systemverilog
if (RL / 2 == RL - LA) begin : g_pds
  always_ff @(posedge clk) if (en) pd <= g_red[k].fbm;      // pacc delayed RL/2, a real FF
end else begin : g_pdl
  otpu_delay #(.W(32), .N(RL / 2)) u_pd (.clk, .en, .d(pacc[k]), .q(pd));
end
```
(Or expose `fbm` as a per-lane array `f32_t fbm [LANES]` declared next to `pacc`.) `fbm` now
fans out to two FFs (`prev`, `pd`), so the SRL chain ends at `fbm` and neither FF can join it.
`pd[k] = fbm[k-1] = pacc[k-(RL-LA)] = pacc[k-RL/2]`, which is identical. This also deletes the 8×32 u_pd
SRLs.

### (c) Lane fmadd c operand: sync reset on `rc` (long and short lanes)

```systemverilog
always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
  if (en) begin ra <= ia; rb <= ib; sr <= sin_; dr <= dest; nr <= negd; end
  // the reset keeps rc out of a shift-register LUT with the fmadd's c delay (r[0], qr: 2 < minlen 3)
  if (rst) rc <= F_NZ; else if (en) rc <= ic_;
end
```
(the same in g_slane). `rc` only differs right after reset, when no valid entry is in any
lane (mo.v needs issued meta) and nothing it computes is written. The reset value F_NZ is
also the idle value of ic_. With `rc` an FDRE(R) the u_c chain is only `r[0], qr`, so it
stays in FFs and `cd` reaches fp_add_s1 from an FDRE.

Nothing else changes: same adders, the same operand order and rounding, the same latency and
schedule, and no protocol change.

## Expected

* Removed from the critical class: about 1.17 ns (SRL clk->Q minus FDRE clk->Q) on u_acc, u_tree
  and the fmadd c legs, plus 0.41 ns (the LUT5 mux) on u_acc. Those paths drop from 5.41 to
  about 4.2–4.3 ns. The next wall is probably the 4.3–4.6 ns class (about 1700 endpoints). Estimated logic
  4.6–4.9 ns, i.e. **est fmax about 118–125 MHz (+8–15%)**. It clears the 110 target and the +3% bar.
* Area (area-eq = LUT + LUTRAM + 0.5 FF):
  - (a) +256 FF (prev), −256 LUT5 muxes when the clear goes on R: about 0 (worst +128)
  - (b) −256 SRL (u_pd), +256 FF (pd): −128
  - (c) if `rc` was SRL-packed: −832 SRL, +1664 FF (rc, r[0] now FFs): +416; if Yosys had
    already inferred a const-srst on rc, about 0
  - net: about −128 to +416 → **−0.3% … +0.9%**, within the +1% the fmax rule allows.
* LUT about −250..−500 (muxes), LUT-RAM −256..−1088, FF +512..+2176.

## Risks

* If shregmap's minlen were 2, the `r[0], qr` pair in (c) could still pack. Then (c) gives
  nothing on the fmadd leg, and if that leg is really at 5.4 ns the gain shrinks to ~0. (I'm fairly
  confident synth_xilinx uses `-minlen 3`.)
* (c) could push area over +1% if the (a)/(b) savings don't materialise (e.g. `prev`'s clear
  lands in a per-bit LUT instead of on R). If so, drop (c) for the long-lane slots ≥ 2, where
  ic_ is a constant per function, and keep it on slots 0/1 and the short lanes.
* The reset on `rc` adds about 830 loads to `rst`. The logic-only Yosys STA doesn't see this, but a real
  P&R replicates it.
* Generate fallbacks: (a) needs RL > LA and (b) needs RL/2 == RL-LA. Both hold for LANES=8, and
  the other LANES values keep the old structure, so lint for other params stays clean.
* Bit-exactness depends on `first_e` being exactly one granted cycle ahead of `mtq.first`.
  It's derived from the same m0 register with an otpu_delay of LM-1 under the same `en`, so it holds by
  construction. The existing `$fatal` schedule check is unchanged.
implementation:
# SRL clock-to-out off the fadd inputs (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)

- (a) RSUM/RSSQ loop: `u_fb` is now `N = RL-LA-1` into a per-lane array `fbm[LANES]`, followed by a
  registered `prev <= first_e ? F_ZERO : fbm[l]`. `first_e` is `m0.first` delayed LM-1 (new `u_fe`),
  i.e. `mtq.first` one granted cycle early. For RL <= LA (LANES=16) `g_fbw` keeps the old combinational form.
- (b) Tree level 0: if RL/2 == RL-LA (LANES=8), `pd <= fbm[k]` is a single FF and replaces the `u_pd`
  SRL line. Otherwise `g_pdl` keeps `u_pd`. `fbm` goes through a flat array, not a cross-generate hierarchical reference.
- (c) Lane fmadd `rc` (long and short lanes) now has a sync reset to F_NZ (the idle value of ic_).
  The other operand registers keep their reset-free `if (en)` form.
- Checks: full-design lint is clean, and so is `otpu_vpu` lint at LANES=4 and 16. Passed: test_mlp_rtl[1],
  test_fuzz_single_slice[0,1], test_lane_count_does_not_change_results[4,16],
  test_board_memory_path_fuzz[0-40] (grant stalls).
- Reviewer: whether shregmap actually leaves `prev`, `pd` and `rc` alone is a synthesis question.
  Confirm it in the netlist (no SRL16E driving u_acc/u_tree a or fmadd cd).
lesson: Replacing the SRL last stage of u_fb/u_pd/fmadd-c with real FFs (sync-clear prev) gave only +1.1% fmax at +1.0% area; SRL clk->Q wasn't the limiter, fp_add_s1 LUT/carry depth is.

title: Lane-level fold: level 2 runs on the level-1 adders (-2 fadds, same latency) + FF-fed RSUM loop/tree operands
hypothesis:
# Lane-level fold: level 2 runs on the level-1 adders (-2 fadds, same latency) + FF-fed RSUM loop/tree operands

Category: area (with the timing fix needed to reach 110 MHz)

## Motivation

- **Area.** The RSUM/RSSQ lane levels (`g_xl`) have LANES-1 = 7 `otpu_fadd`s: 4 for level 1,
  2 for level 2, 1 for the root. Each adder is used **once per row**, and rows are at least RL = 8
  granted cycles apart. Level 1 issues at offset 0 (relative to the last row level's result),
  level 2 at offset LA = 4 and the root at 2·LA = 8. Rows start a multiple of RL cycles apart
  (the header comment and the `$fatal` collision check both guarantee this). So a level-1 adder is
  free at every offset ≡ 4 (mod 8), which is exactly when level 2 needs an adder. The two level-2
  adders are therefore redundant hardware. An fp32 adder here is about 400–450 LUTs plus 192 FFs
  (p1 76 b, p2 42 b, nm 42 b, r 32 b), so about 520 area-equivalent each.
- **Timing.** The critical path (5.412 ns, 109 MHz) starts at an **SRL16E clock-to-out
  (1472 ps)** on `g_red[7].u_fb.g_regs.qr`. That is the `otpu_delay`'s "last stage is a flip-flop",
  but Yosys `xilinx_srl` absorbed it anyway: the `keep`/`shreg_extract` attributes are on the wire,
  not on the FF cell. The path then goes through the `mtq.first ? 0 : fb` LUT5 (+407 ps) into
  `fp_add_s1` (compare/swap carry chain, exponent subtract). The tree's `u_pd` has the same shape
  (4-deep SRL → 3:1 `oa` mux → `fp_add_s1`), and so do all 8 lanes of each. That is the ~390
  endpoints in the top histogram bin. An FDRE clk→Q is about 0.3 ns, so this class of path gets
  about 1.1–1.5 ns shorter.

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)

### 1. Share the level-2 lane adders (generate-guarded)

The sharing is enabled by `localparam bit SH2 = (LW >= 2) && (LA % RL != 0);`. It is true for
LANES = 8 (RL = 8) and LANES = 4, and false for LANES = 16, where RL = LA and every offset
collides, so that configuration keeps the old structure.

- **Strobe.** Add `wire l2_v = rsr[DL + 2*LA - 1];`. `rsr[DL-1]` marks the last row level's issue
  cycle, so level 1 issues at `DL+LA-1` and level 2 at `DL+2LA-1`. This matches
  `root_v = rsr[RD-1]` with `RD = DL + LA*(1+LW)`.
- **Level-1 adders, k < LANES>>2.** Their operands become
  `a = l2_v ? xl[1][k] : xl[0][k]` and
  `b = l2_v ? xl[1][k + (LANES>>2)] : xl[0][k + (LANES>>1)]`. Their own registered output
  `xl[1][k]` is `r`, an FF, so there is no combinational loop.
- **Level 2.** Its `otpu_fadd`s are not instantiated. Instead, `xl[2][k] = xl[1][k]` (alias), and
  level 3 onward (the root for LANES = 8) reads `xl[2]` exactly as before.
- **Why it stays bit-exact.**
  - Every addition is the same `fp_add` with the same `a`/`b` operand order:
    `xl2[k] = xl1[k] + xl1[k+2]` and `root = xl2[0] + xl2[1]`, which is the isum_64 / docs/isa.md
    order.
  - Each value is produced on the same cycle as before, so `root_v`, `RD`, `wr_row` and `done`
    timing are unchanged. There is **zero added latency**, so the Qwen3 decode proxy and the
    attention_decode gate are unaffected.
  - A level-2 issue at T+LA can never meet a level-1 issue of another row, which happens at
    T + m·RL, because LA mod RL ≠ 0. The garbage computed in idle cycles is never observed,
    since only `root_v` samples the output.

### 2. RSUM loop operand from a resettable FF, with the `first` zeroing folded into it

- **`g_red`.** When `RL - LA >= 1`:
  - Shorten `u_fb` to `N = RL-LA-1`, producing `fbd`.
  - Delay `m0.first` by LM-1 cycles with `otpu_delay #(.W(1), .N(LM-1))`, producing `first_e`.
  - Add `always_ff if (en) fbq <= first_e ? F_ZERO : fbd;` and set `prev = fbq`.
  - Why it is identical: `first_e` one cycle before is `mtq.first`, and `fbq(t) = pacc(t-(RL-LA))`
    or `+0`, which is exactly the old `prev`.
  - Why it helps: the sync clear makes it an FDRE with R, which `xilinx_srl` cannot absorb.
    The mux LUT disappears from the D path, and u_acc's `a` input comes straight from an FF.
  - The R pin is `en & first_e`, a single shared LUT2. Gating it with `en` keeps the frozen-grant
    behaviour: `fbq` holds while `gnt` is low.
- **Tree `pd`.** Give `pd` a last stage with a sync `rst` reset. This makes it unabsorbable at
  no LUT cost, since `rst` has priority over `en`, which matches FDRE. Its value after reset is
  don't-care, just as the delay lines are uninitialised.
  - When `RL/2 == RL - LA` (LANES = 8), `pd`'s FF loads from the same `fbd` SRL. The separate
    `u_pd` delay line is deleted.
  - Otherwise, keep `otpu_delay #(.N(RL/2-1))` + the reset FF.
  - To feed it, expose `fbd` per lane through a module-level `f32_t` array.

## Expected

| Item | LUT | LUT-RAM | FF | Area-eq |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| −2 fadds | −800…−900 | | −384 | |
| + 2:1 operand muxes on 2 adders | +128 | | | |
| fb mux removed (partly merged into `fp_add_s1` today) | −100…−256 | | +256 | |
| `u_pd` SRLs removed (LANES = 8) | | −256 | +256 | |
| **Net** | about −850 | −256 | +130 | **about −1050 (≈ −2.2%)** |

- **fmax.** The SRL→mux→`fp_add_s1` class (u_acc and u_tree, top bin 5.15–5.42 ns) drops to about
  4.0–4.3 ns. The next bin tops out at 5.149 ns, so logic is ≤ 5.15 ns. That is est. fmax of about
  **113–115 MHz** (≥ 110 target).
- **Remaining limiter.** Probably the meta SRL (`mtap`) → `wtap`/`mo` → `lres` → `cw_*` path.
  The two muxed level-1 adders take their inputs from FFs, so they gain one LUT level but lose
  the 1.1 ns SRL penalty and stay off-critical.

## Risks

- **Schedule collision for other parameterisations.** A level-2 issue could land on a level-1
  issue of the next row. The `SH2` guard (`LA % RL != 0`) and the existing `$fatal` collision
  check cover this. Adding a sim assertion that `l2_v` never coincides with a level-1 issue
  (`rsr[DL+LA-1]`) would be cheap.
- **Operand order.** The level-2 operand mux must keep lower index → `a` and higher index → `b`.
  `fp_add` is commutative bit-exactly (the swap on magnitude, the ties keep `a`, cancellation
  gives +0, the NaN is canonical), but the order is kept anyway.
- **Off-by-one timing.**
  - Aligning `first_e`: it needs LM-1 = 1 cycle, and `mtq` is an LM-cycle delay of `m0r`.
  - The `l2_v` tap index.
  - Either error gives wrong RSUM/RSSQ sums, which the bit-exact tests would catch immediately.
- **Yosys might still merge `pd`'s FF into an SRL.** It has a reset, so `xilinx_srl` should skip
  it. If the fmax gain doesn't show, the next thing to check is whether any `SRL16E` still
  drives `fp_add_s1`.
- **LUT estimate.** If an fadd is smaller than estimated (for example 300 LUTs), the area gain
  shrinks to about −1.5%, which is still ≥ 1%.
implementation:
# Implementation: lane-level fold sharing + FF-fed RSUM loop/tree operands

Changed `rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv` only, as described in HYPOTHESIS.md:
- **Level-2 sharing (`SH2 = LW >= 2 && LA % RL != 0`).** This is true for LANES = 4 and 8 and false for 16.
  - The level-1 adders k < LANES/4 (`g_xl[1].g_k[k].g_mux`) now take `l2_v ? {xs[k], xl[1][k+LANES/4]} : {xl[0][k], xl[0][k+LANES/2]}`, where `l2_v = rsr[DL+2*LA-1]`.
  - Level 2 is aliased (`xl[2][k] = xs[k]`).
  - Their result goes through a separate array `xs`. Writing `xl[2][k] = xl[1][k]` directly made Verilator report a false UNOPTFLAT loop on `xl`.
  - A new `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$fatal` fires if `l2_v` ever coincides with a level-1 issue.
- **RSUM loop.** `u_fb` is now `RL-LA-1` deep (`fbd[l]`, a module-level array). A new FF, `fbq <= first_e ? +0 : fbd`, feeds u_acc's `a` input, where `first_e` is `m0.first` delayed LM-1 by one shared `u_first`. The old mux path (`g_fbw`) is kept for RL == LA (LANES = 16).
- **Tree `pd`.** The last stage is an FF with a sync `rst` reset. When RL/2 == RL-LA (LANES = 8), it loads from `fbd[k]` and `u_pd` is gone. Otherwise it keeps `u_pd` at N = RL/2-1.
- **Checks.** Lint is clean at LANES = 8, 4 and 16. These tests pass: `test_mlp_rtl[1]`, `test_lane_count_does_not_change_results[4,16]`, and `fuzz_single_slice` + `scoreboard_stress_single_slice` (20 tests, which include RSUM/RSSQ).
- **Reviewer notes.**
  - Hierarchy names changed (`g_xl[q].g_k[k].g_add/g_mux.u_add`, `g_red[l].g_fbq.u_fb`, `g_tree[k].g_pdd.u_pd`), in case any synthesis or timing script refers to them.
  - The fmax/area gain depends on Yosys keeping `fbq`/`pd` as FDRE rather than absorbing them into SRLs. That is still unverified here.
lesson: Accepted: level-2 lane fadds share the level-1 adders (level 2 fires at offset LA mod RL, when level 1 is idle; bit-exact, no added latency). Area -1.9%, but 110 MHz is only +0.6%.

title: Fixed end taps for the lane results (kill the false `fp_max -> st[wtap] -> EXP2 adder` path) + pre-muxed B operand
hypothesis:
# Fixed end taps for the lane results (kill the false `fp_max -> st[wtap] -> EXP2 adder` path) + pre-muxed B operand

Category: timing

## Motivation

The champion's critical path (5.378 ns, 110 MHz) is a **false path**. Decoding it against the RTL:

- It starts at `\m0 [85]`. In `meta_t`, counted from the LSB: sub[7:0], final_ 8, first 9, all_last 10,
  row_last 11, waddr[43:12], mask[51:44], imm[83:52], **bmode[85:84]**, so `m0[85]` is `m0.bmode[1]`.
- 399 -> 1030 -> 1661 ps: two LUT5s at 631 ps each. Each costs that much because of fanout: `m0.bmode`
  feeds every lane's `y = (bmode==B_SCALAR) ? imm : (bmode==B_ROW) ? xb[0] : xb[l]`, and `y`
  feeds everything downstream.
- 1661 -> 3373 ps: LUTs and a CARRY4 chain (`$5016`, sum output). This is `fkey`/`fp_gt` inside
  `fp_max`/`fp_min(x, y)`, which computes `st[0].v`.
- 3373 -> 4262 ps: a LUT3/LUT3/LUT3/LUT2 chain. This is the 11-way `t = st[wtap]` mux in the long
  lanes' result block (a 4-bit select `wtap` over 11 taps).
- 4262 -> 5124 ps: an `alumacc` CARRY4 pair (S->CO, CI->O) plus a LUT4. This is the EXP2 exponent add
  `t.v + {t.ii, 23'd0}`. It adds bits [31:23], so it is 3 CARRY4s.
- 5378 ps: LUT6 (dffopt enable merge) into an FDRE, i.e. `lres -> cw_data -> tw_data`.

EXP2's result never comes from tap 0. EXP2 always ends at tap 9 (`n_slots == 9`), so `st[0].v`
(the MAX/MIN/COPY/ABS/FILL value) never reaches the EXP2 adder. Synthesis can't prove this: `mo.func`
and `wtap` are two separately decoded signals, and `wtap` is a 4-bit select. So the tool times
compare + 11-way mux + adder + result mux as one path, about 2 ns of logic that never happens.
The r20260924-032708-s0 "fixed end taps" idea got 112 MHz and -1.4% area on an older base. It
lost its round to the streaming-tree slot, so it was never merged. It's still missing from the
current code (`t = st[wtap]` is still there).

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)

### A. Fixed taps with a priority result select that uses the same order as `wtap`

Add, next to the `wtap/mo` block, one end strobe per tap that can end an entry. Each strobe is decoded
from that tap's own meta, which is a register or delay-line output, not from `wtap`:

```systemverilog
function automatic logic ends_at(input mt_t m, input int s);
  return m.v && !red_f(m.func) && n_slots(m.func) == 4'(s);
endfunction
wire e0 = ends_at(mtap[0], 0), e1 = ends_at(mtap[1], 1), e6 = ends_at(mtap[6], 6),
     e9 = ends_at(mtap[9], 9);
```

Long lanes: replace the `t = st[wtap]; case (mo.func)` block with fixed taps:

```systemverilog
f32_t r_exp2, r_recip, r_rsqrt, r_hi;
assign r_exp2  = st[9].f[0] ? F_ZERO : st[9].f[1] ? F_INF : (st[9].v + {st[9].ii, 23'd0});
assign r_recip = st[6].f[0] ? F_ZERO : st[6].f[1] ? {st[6].f[2], 31'd0}
                                     : (st[6].f[2] ? fneg(st[6].k2) : st[6].k2);
assign r_rsqrt = st[10].f[0] ? F_ZERO : st[10].k2;
// wtap picks the lowest tap that ends an entry: keep that priority, tap 0 last (nearest the output)
assign r_hi    = e1 ? st[1].v : e6 ? r_recip : e9 ? r_exp2 : r_rsqrt;
assign lres[l] = e0 ? st[0].v : r_hi;
```

Short lanes: `assign lres[l] = e0 ? st[0] : st[1];` in place of `(wtap == 0) ? ...`.

`wtap` then has no readers and goes away. Keep `mo` as it is for `cw_en`/`cw_addr`/`all_last`.

**Why the results are bit-identical.** `lres` is only read when `mo.v && mo.mask[l]`. In that case
`wtap` is the lowest s where `mtap[s]` is valid, not a reduction, and `n_slots(func) == s`. Only
s ∈ {0, 1, 6, 9, 10} can match. The new priority chain tests e0, e1, e6, e9 in that order and falls
back to tap 10, so it picks the same tap. It also applies the same function-specific formula,
because `n_slots == 9` ⇔ EXP2/EXP2SUB, `== 6` ⇔ RECIP, `== 10` ⇔ RSQRT, and `== 0/1` ⇔ the `default`
(`t.v`) case. Every formula is the same expression on the same `st[s]` fields. When `mo.v == 0`,
`lres` is masked out of `cw_data` exactly as before. Short lanes never carry composite functions
(`imask` stops at `iwid = NCL`), so their end tap is 0 or 1 and `e0` selects the same way `wtap == 0`
does.

### B. Register the B operand already muxed (`yb` replaces `xb`)

`xb` is only read through `y`. Replace `xb <= tb_data` with a per-lane pre-muxed register, loaded
under the same `en` as `m0 <= mi`:

```systemverilog
for (int l = 0; l < LANES; l++)
  yb[l] <= (mi.bmode == B_SCALAR) ? mi.imm : (mi.bmode == B_ROW) ? tb_data[0] : tb_data[l];
```

In both lane generates, use `assign y = yb[l];`. `m0`, `xb` and `yb` all load from `mi`/`tb_data`
under the same enable, so `yb[l]` always equals the old `y` (tb_data[0] is read at `b_row` in
B_ROW mode, as before). The mux needs 5 inputs (imm bit, tb_data[0] bit, tb_data[l] bit, 2 bmode
bits), so it fits one LUT5 before the FF. It is fed by `mi` FFs, so on the new path the input port
goes through a single LUT. `m0.bmode`/`m0.imm` become dead in `m0` (34 FFs, plus the 631 ps fanout
nets). The FF count for `yb` equals the `xb` it replaces.

## Expected

- Critical path: the false EXP2 leg disappears (about -0.9 ns: the wtap mux and the 3-CARRY4 add).
  Registering `y` removes the two high-fanout LUT5 hops (about -1.2 ns). The real tap-0 path becomes
  yb FF -> fkey/fp_gt carry -> select -> `e0` mux -> cw_data -> tw_data, about 3.5–4 ns. The next
  limiter should be an adder stage (fp_add s1 in u_tree/u_acc/fmadd), which the lessons put at about
  5.1–5.2 ns. Estimated fmax 113–116 MHz (+3–5%).
- LUT: -300 to -600. The 11-way × 108-bit (live fields) `st[wtap]` mux in 2 long lanes becomes a
  5-way × 32-bit priority mux. The y mux moves but stays the same size.
- FF: -34 (dead m0.bmode/imm). DSP/BRAM unchanged. Area-equivalent about -0.7% to -1.5%.

## Risks

- If the tap invariant (at most one entry ends per cycle, enforced by `can_begin`) were violated, a
  plain AND-OR would differ. The priority order above matches `wtap` exactly, so this doesn't apply.
- Part B puts one LUT after `tb_data` (TMEM read data) before the register. The OOC judge doesn't see
  it, but in the full slice the TMEM read-mux-to-VPU path gains one LUT (it still ends in an FF, not
  in a DSP, so the spirit of the "no BRAM -> multiplier in one cycle" comment holds). If board-level
  timing complains, keep only part A.
- The fixed-tap numbers (1, 6, 9, 10) are tied to `n_slots`. Add a comment there, and a
  `ifndef SYNTHESIS` assertion that `wtap ∈ {0,1,6,9,10}` whenever `mo.v`, to catch future edits.
- If the next critical path (fadd s1) is already at about 5.2 ns, the fmax gain could land between
  +2% and +3%. Area should still drop, but maybe by less than 1%.

# Implementation: fixed end taps + pre-muxed B operand (rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv only)

- A: removed `wtap` / `t = st[wtap]; case (mo.func)`. Added `ends_at(mt_t, s)` (shared with the `mo` loop) and end strobes `et0/et1/et6/et9`, each decoded from its own `mtap[s]`. Long lanes: fixed-tap formulas `r_exp2` (st[9]), `r_recip` (st[6]), `r_rsqrt` (st[10]); `lres = et0 ? st[0].v : et1 ? st[1].v : et6 ? r_recip : et9 ? r_exp2 : r_rsqrt`, which is the same lowest-tap-first priority as the old `wtap`. Short lanes: `lres = et0 ? st[0] : st[1]`.
- The strobes are named `et*`, not `e*` as in the hypothesis, because `g_slot[1].g_pre` already has local regs `e1`/`e2`.
- `mo` is unchanged (`cw_en`/`cw_addr`/`all_last`).
- B: `xb` replaced by `yb[l]`, loaded under the same `en` as `m0 <= mi` with the bmode mux applied to `mi`/`tb_data`. Both lane generates use `assign y = yb[l]`. `m0.bmode`/`m0.imm` are now dead (left in `meta_t` because `mi` still needs them; synthesis trims them).
- Added a comment on `n_slots` about the fixed taps, and an `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$fatal` if an elementwise `mo` ends at a tap outside {0,1,6,9,10}.
- Checks: verilator lint is clean (no warnings). These passed: `test_mlp_rtl[1]`, `test_fuzz_single_slice` (all seeds; covers EXP2/RECIP/RSQRT and all B modes) and `test_lane_count_does_not_change_results`.
- Risk (from the hypothesis): part B puts one LUT between `tb_data` and the `yb` register. It still ends in an FF, but check full-slice timing on the TMEM read path.
lesson: Fixed end taps (per-tap ends_at strobes replacing the 11-way st[wtap] mux) plus a pre-muxed B operand gave only +1.8% fmax and -0.4% area, so it was no gain. Removing the false fp_max->EXP2 path isn't enough by itself.

# Long-lane results from fixed end taps: remove the 11-way `st[wtap]` mux and the false `m0 -> fp_max -> EXP2 adder -> tw_data` path

Category: timing (and area)

## Motivation
The champion's critical path (5.378 ns) runs:

`m0[85]` (bit 85 of meta_t is `bmode[1]`) -> `y` mux (`B_SCALAR/B_ROW/B_FULL`) -> `fp_max/fp_min`
of boundary 0 (`ftz`, `fkey`, compare carry chain `$5016`) -> `st[0].v` -> the long lane's
`t = st[wtap]` mux (the LUT3/LUT3/LUT3/LUT2 run) -> the EXP2 end adder `t.v + {t.ii, 23'd0}`
(2-slice chain `alumacc 40016`, sum bits [30:27]) -> the `lres` / `cw_data` mux (LUT4) ->
`tw_data` FF (LUT6 from dffopt, the `gnt` enable).

This path can't actually happen. EXP2/EXP2SUB always end at tap 9, but `lres` in `g_lane` reads
`st[wtap]` for every function, so synthesis has to route every boundary (0..10) into the EXP2
adder. That includes boundary 0, which is combinational from the TMEM read registers through
`fp_max`. The RECIP (tap 6) and RSQRT (tap 10) legs are also muxed over all 11 boundaries.
Round r20260924-032708-s0 tried this fix ("Fixed end taps for the composite results"). It
reached 112 MHz with area -1.4%, and was reported as *improvement*. It never reached this
branch: the streaming fold tree won that round, and the current `otpu_vpu.sv` still has
`t = st[wtap]`. The fold-tree read path that also needed fixing back then was removed by the
streaming tree, so this change is enough on its own now.

## Change (only rtl/vpu/otpu_vpu.sv)
1. **Hit flags per tap.** An entry can end only at the taps {0, 1, 6, 9, 10}, because
   `n_slots` ∈ {0, 1, 6, 9, 10}. So work out `hit[s] = mtap[s].v && !red_f(mtap[s].func) &&
   n_slots(mtap[s].func) == s` for those five taps only. The priority loop that builds `mo`
   (and `wtap`, if we keep it) runs over the same five taps, lowest `s` first as today.
   `mo` is unchanged, because an entry never matches at any other tap.
2. **Long lanes (`g_lane`)**: replace the `st[wtap]` + `case (mo.func)` block with fixed taps:
   ```
   e9 = st[9];  r6 = st[6];  q10 = st[10];
   exp2_r  = e9.f[0] ? F_ZERO : e9.f[1] ? F_INF : (e9.v + {e9.ii, 23'd0});
   recip_r = r6.f[0] ? F_ZERO : r6.f[1] ? {r6.f[2], 31'd0} : (r6.f[2] ? fneg(r6.k2) : r6.k2);
   rsqrt_r = q10.f[0] ? F_ZERO : q10.k2;
   lres[l] = hit[9] ? exp2_r : hit[6] ? recip_r : hit[10] ? rsqrt_r : hit[0] ? st[0].v : st[1].v;
   ```
   These are the same formulas as today, applied to the same boundary each function already
   ends at (`wtap == n_slots(func)`).
3. **Short lanes (`g_slane`)**: `lres[l] = hit[0] ? st[0] : st[1]`. Same as `wtap == 0`,
   because an entry at tap 0 is exactly `hit[0]`.

**Why it stays bit-exact:** when `mo.v` is set, exactly one tap `s` hits, `wtap == s`, and
`mo.func`'s case arm is the function that ends at `s`. The new selection returns that arm on
`st[s]`, which is the value used today. When nothing hits, `cw_en` for the lanes is 0 and
`lres` is ignored, same as today. No latency, schedule, protocol, rounding or operation-order
changes. It's a purely combinational restructure of the result select.

## Expected
